answer: A sybil farm needs cheap copies, so make copies expensive: every claim must be signed by an address that already settled real work, which means a fake identity costs the whole proof chain again, not one spare keypair. A falcon takes one prey at a time; the ledger does the same, weighing each claim against its own history at dawn, before the epoch closes. An identity scattered over a tundra of fresh wallets earns nothing until it has walked a path.
